### cognito-alb-authenticate-cognito-https-only

**Claim.** An Application Load Balancer can authenticate users before they reach the application, through an OIDC-compliant IdP or through Cognito user pools (social IdPs and corporate SAML, OIDC or OAuth identities); the authenticate-cognito and authenticate-oidc actions are supported only on HTTPS listeners.

> "The `authenticate-cognito` and `authenticate-oidc` action types are supported only with HTTPS listeners."

### cognito-api-gateway-cognito-user-pools-authorizer

**Write it as.** `an authorizer of the `COGNITO_USER_POOLS` type` · `supply the appropriate token in the `Authorization` header` · `the supplied token is valid`

**Scope.** API Gateway REST APIs.

> — [Control access to REST APIs using Amazon Cognito user pools as an authorizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-integrate-with-cognito.html)

> "The API call succeeds only if the required token is supplied and the supplied token is valid, otherwise, the client isn't authorized to make the call because the client did not have credentials that could be authorized."

### cognito-identity-pool-trust-policy-aud-condition-enforced

**Write it as.** `permit any identity pool to assume the role` · `but `aud` is required` · `IAM returns an error`

**Scope.** IAM roles trusted by Cognito identity pools.

> "Where the `Principal` of an IAM role trust policy is an identity pools service principal like `cognito-identity.amazonaws.com`, you can't create or modify role trust policies such that they permit any identity pool to assume the role. With the identity pool principal, the `Action` element must have a `Condition` that requires that `AssumeRoleWithWebIndentity` be performed only by your identity pools, as specified by a condition key like `cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud`. Other condition keys are available, but `aud` is required."
> — [IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/iam-roles.html)

> "If you attempt to save a role trust policy without a condition of this type, IAM returns an error."
> — [IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/iam-roles.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-refresh-token-rotation-behavior

When this setting is disabled, token-refresh requests return new access and ID tokens only and the original refresh token remains valid. The new refresh token is valid for the remaining duration of the original refresh token."

> "To allow for retries for a brief duration, you can also configure a grace period for the original refresh token of up to 60 seconds."

### cognito-token-revocation-enabled-by-default

**Claim.** Token revocation is enabled by default when a new user pool app client is created, and refresh tokens can be revoked only in app clients with token revocation enabled.

**Write it as.** `token revocation is enabled by default` · `only in app clients with token revocation enabled`

**Scope.** per Cognito user pool app client; default; adjustable; new user pool clients.

> "+ When you create a new user pool client, token revocation is enabled by default."
> — [Ending user sessions with token revocation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/token-revocation.html)

> "+ You can revoke refresh tokens only in app clients with token revocation enabled."
> — [Ending user sessions with token revocation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/token-revocation.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-token-revocation-refresh-token-and-global-signout

**Claim.** Revoking a refresh token invalidates all access tokens issued from it; GlobalSignOut (authorized by the user's access token) and AdminUserGlobalSignOut (authorized by an administrator's IAM credentials) revoke all of a user's refresh, ID and access tokens; revoked JWTs still pass a check by any JWT library that only verifies signature and expiration.

**Write it as.** `issued by that refresh token become invalid` · `target user's refresh, ID, and access tokens` · `revoked tokens will still be valid`

**Scope.** Cognito user pool tokens; token revocation enabled on the app client.

> "When you revoke a refresh token, all access tokens that were previously issued by that refresh token become invalid."
> — [Ending user sessions with token revocation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/token-revocation.html)

> "AdminUserGlobalSignOut is a server-side operation that an administrator authorizes with IAM credentials. This operation revokes all of the target user's refresh, ID, and access tokens."
> — [Ending user sessions with token revocation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/token-revocation.html)

> "Revoked tokens can't be used with any Amazon Cognito API calls that require a token. However, revoked tokens will still be valid if they are verified using any JWT library that verifies the signature and expiration of the token."
> — [Ending user sessions with token revocation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/token-revocation.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-unauthenticated-role-more-restrictive

**Claim.** An identity pool can have default IAM roles for authenticated and unauthenticated users; the unauthenticated identities are assumed by users who do not log in, so their permissions should typically be more restrictive than those for authenticated identities.

**Write it as.** `default IAM roles for authenticated and unauthenticated users` · `should be more restrictive`

**Scope.** Cognito identity pool roles.

> "You can specify default IAM roles for authenticated and unauthenticated users."
> — [IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/iam-roles.html)

> "Remember that unauthenticated identities are assumed by users who do not log in to your app. Typically, the permissions that you assign for unauthenticated identities should be more restrictive than those for authenticated identities."
> — [IAM roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/iam-roles.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-user-migration-jit-lambda-no-reset

**Claim.** Users move into Cognito user pools by just-in-time migration or bulk migration; the just-in-time Lambda trigger migrates users at sign-in without forcing a password reset.

**Write it as.** `just-in-time (JIT) migration and bulk migration` · `without forcing them to reset their password`

**Scope.** migrating users into a Cognito user pool; just-in-time migration with the Lambda trigger.

> "There are two ways you can migrate users from your application's existing user directory or database to user pools: just-in-time (JIT) migration and bulk migration."
> — [FAQs | Amazon Cognito | Amazon Web Services (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/cognito/faqs/)

> "The Lambda trigger enables you to migrate users’ data from an external system without forcing them to reset their password."
> — [FAQs | Amazon Cognito | Amazon Web Services (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/cognito/faqs/)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-user-pool-federated-users-get-profile-and-jwt

**Claim.** Federated and local users both have a user profile in the user pool; the user pool accepts tokens and assertions from third-party IdPs and collects the user attributes into a JWT that it issues to the app, so the app works with one set of JWTs.

**Write it as.** `Federated and local users have a user profile` · `collect the user attributes into a JWT` · `standardize your app on one set of JWTs`

**Scope.** Cognito user pool federation.

> "With a user pool, your users can sign in to your web or mobile app through Amazon Cognito, or federate through a third-party IdP. Federated and local users have a user profile in your user pool."
> — [What is Amazon Cognito?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/what-is-amazon-cognito.html)

> "Amazon Cognito user pools accept tokens and assertions from third-party IdPs, and collect the user attributes into a JWT that it issues to your app. You can standardize your app on one set of JWTs while Amazon Cognito handles the interactions with IdPs, mapping their claims to a central token format."
> — [What is Amazon Cognito?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/what-is-amazon-cognito.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-user-pool-federation-independent-of-identity-pool

**Claim.** Sign-in through a third-party IdP is a feature of Cognito user pools and is independent of federation through identity pools, which must be set up separately in each identity pool; a user pool can be a third-party IdP to an identity pool.

**Write it as.** `independent of federation through Amazon Cognito identity pools` · `third-party IdP to an identity pool`

**Scope.** Cognito federation.

> "Sign-in through a third party (federation) is available in Amazon Cognito user pools. This feature is independent of federation through Amazon Cognito identity pools (federated identities)."
> — [User pool sign-in with third party identity providers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-identity-federation.html)

> "Amazon Cognito identity pools, sometimes called Amazon Cognito federated identities, are an implementation of federation that you must set up separately in each identity pool. A user pool can be a third-party IdP to an identity pool."
> — [Using SAML identity providers with a user pool](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-saml-idp.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-user-pool-sp-and-idp-dual-role

**Claim.** A Cognito user pool can act both as a service provider to external IdPs and as an IdP to your app, connecting to consumer IdPs such as Facebook and Google or workforce IdPs such as Okta and AD FS.

**Write it as.** `a dual role as a service provider (SP)` · `consumer IdPs like Facebook and Google` · `workforce IdPs like Okta`

**Scope.** Cognito user pool federation.

> "An Amazon Cognito user pool can also fulfill a dual role as a service provider (SP) to your IdPs, and an IdP to your app. Amazon Cognito user pools can connect to consumer IdPs like Facebook and Google, or workforce IdPs like Okta and Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS)."
> — [What is Amazon Cognito?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/what-is-amazon-cognito.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-user-pool-vs-identity-pool

**Claim.** A Cognito user pool is a user directory that authenticates users and issues JSON web tokens to your app or API; a Cognito identity pool exchanges a trusted token for temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials so the app can call AWS services on the user's behalf.

**Write it as.** `issue JSON web tokens (JWTs)` · `temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials`

**Scope.** Cognito user pools and identity pools.

> "A user pool is a user directory that draws from the OpenID Connect (OIDC) standard to authenticate users and issue JSON web tokens (JWTs) to your app or API."
> — [What is Amazon Cognito?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/what-is-amazon-cognito.html)

> "An identity pool exchanges a trusted token (from a user pool, a social provider, or a SAML or OIDC provider) for temporary, limited-privilege AWS credentials so that your app can call services like Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB on the user's behalf."
> — [What is Amazon Cognito?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/what-is-amazon-cognito.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-user-pool-workforce-sso-in-your-app

**Claim.** With user pools you can provide single sign-on in your app for an organization's workforce identities in SAML 2.0 and OIDC IdPs, and for customer identities from Amazon, Google, Apple and Facebook.

**Write it as.** `workforce identities in SAML 2.0 and OIDC IdPs` · `Amazon, Google, Apple and Facebook`

**Scope.** Cognito user pool federation.

> "You can provide single sign-on (SSO) in your app for your organization's workforce identities in SAML 2.0 and OIDC IdPs with user pools. You can also provide SSO in your app for your organization's customer identities in the public OAuth 2.0 identity stores Amazon, Google, Apple and Facebook."
> — [What is Amazon Cognito?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/what-is-amazon-cognito.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### cognito-user-pools-billed-by-mau

**Claim.** Cognito user pools are billed by monthly active users (MAUs): a user counts once in a calendar month when an identity operation such as sign-up, sign-in, sign-out, token refresh or password change happens for that user; inactive users are not charged.

**Write it as.** `monthly active users (MAUs)` · `not charged for subsequent sessions`

**Scope.** per calendar month.

> "You pay for Amazon Cognito user pools based on your monthly active users (MAUs). A user is counted as a MAU if, within a calendar month, your app generates an identity operation for that user, like administrative creation or update, sign-up, sign-in, sign-out, token refresh, password change, a user account attribute update, or an attribute query on a user (AdminGetUser API). You are not charged for subsequent sessions or for inactive users within that calendar month."
> — [FAQs | Amazon Cognito | Amazon Web Services (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/cognito/faqs/)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.
